source.name: Game Code Check
source.instructions: Click Check It to have your game code evaluated. The autograder will check for the core mechanics you've learned in this unit.

rubrics.title: Player Actor with keyboard input
rubrics.description: Game has a player Actor that moves with keyboard input (e.g., arrow keys or WASD)

rubrics.title: Screen boundaries
rubrics.description: Player stays within screen boundaries and cannot move off-screen

rubrics.title: Additional Actor interaction
rubrics.description: Game includes at least one other Actor that the player interacts with (collectible, enemy, obstacle)

rubrics.title: Collision detection
rubrics.description: Collision detection works using colliderect() or similar collision method

rubrics.title: Score or lives tracking
rubrics.description: Game tracks score or lives using a global variable

rubrics.title: Game states
rubrics.description: Game has at least two states (e.g., start and playing, or playing and game over)

rubrics.title: Text display
rubrics.description: Game displays text on screen (score, instructions, or game over message) using screen.draw.text()

rubrics.title: Code runs without errors
rubrics.description: Code is syntactically correct and would run without Python errors

source.rubricsRequirements: This is a PyGame Zero game. Students are building a complete game from scratch using Actor objects, keyboard input, collision detection, score tracking, game states, and text display. Evaluate the code in game.py against each rubric item.
